text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - British stocks ended a nervous election day session Thursday with a closing record but by the slimmest of margins as many investors stayed away ahead of the ballot result, which is due early Friday. The FTSE 100 index closed 9.0 points higher at a new peak of 4,445.0, only 0.7 points above the previous all-time high of 4,444.3, reached March 11.
FRANKFURT - The German stock market was closed Thursday for a market holiday. On Wednesday, the DAX-30 index of leading German stocks ended the session up 54.88 points at 3,438.07.
PARIS - The French stock market was closed Thursday for a market holiday. On Wednesday, the CAC-40 index closed up 36.60 points at 2639.46.
ZURICH - The Swiss stock market was closed Thursday for a market holiday. On Wednesday, the Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 23.70 points at 3,094.65.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended modestly higher Thursday supported by buying of some major issues after early gains on buying of blue chips were eroded by profit-taking, brokers said. They said gains in recent sessions were too rapid and the indices needed to take a breather. The 225-share Nikkei average closed 124.21 points higher at 19,275.33.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks rose steeply for the second day in a row Thursday, closing above the 13,000-point level for the first time since mid-March as gains on Wall Street propelled prices higher, brokers said. The blue-chip Hang Seng Index soared 117.48 points, to finish at 13,020.78.

SYDNEY - Local indecision and persistent nervousness over Wall Street's behaviour pushed the Australian stock market slightly lower by the close Thursday. The All Ordinaries index fell 2.6 points to 2,485.4. Continued scepticism over Wall Street's rebound, with key economic data still to come in the United States, compounded by stronger than expected local wage data saw the market endure a day of choppy, range-bound trade with little real direction.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stock markets were closed Thursday for a market holiday. On Wednesday, the overall index ended up 23.5 points at 7,130.5, the industrial index gained 41.5 points to 8,494.3 points, and the gold index dropped 18.2 points to fresh four-year low of 1,187.0 points.
